\section{Results: Quality}
\label{sec:results-quality}

This section reports the quality axis of the study: how much cross-document
attention can be removed before answer quality drops below the parity
band. We report four experiments in cost order: the train-free mask sweep
(the primary result), a conditional fine-tuned sweep, the bridge-width
curve that traces the quality/cost frontier, and a base-versus-instruct
mechanism probe.

\subsection{Train-free and fine-tuned mask sweeps}
\label{sec:results-quality-sweep}

The primary quality result is the train-free sweep: for every combination
of primary model, base/instruct variant, dataset, and mask variant, the
mask is swapped at inference on stock weights and evaluated with $\geq 3$
seeds. If the median gap to \texttt{full} is smaller than the
non-inferiority margin $\Delta$ (Section~\ref{sec:method-delta}) the
train-free result alone supports the parity claim for that cell, and the
fine-tuned sweep becomes confirmatory rather than load-bearing.

Table~\ref{tab:t2} pairs train-free and (where run) fine-tuned quality on
the same cells. Any cell whose train-free row is inside the $\Delta$ band
carries the parity claim without needing the fine-tuned row.

\subsection{Bridge-width curve}
\label{sec:results-quality-bridge}

The \texttt{ddi\_bridge\_k} family (Section~\ref{sec:method-masks})
interpolates between full query--document attention ($k = Q$) and a
single SEP-row bridge ($k = 1$). Sweeping $k$ turns a hypothesised step
function --- ``document isolation is nearly free; query isolation is
catastrophic'' --- into a curve, and locates the knee at which quality
begins to degrade.

\figureifexists{generated/F2.pdf}{%
    F2 --- bridge-width curve. Validation loss (or headline quality
    metric) as a function of the bridge width $k$, on the primary model.
    $k = 1$ is \texttt{ddi\_strict}; $k = Q$ is \texttt{ddi\_qf}.%
}{fig:f2}

\subsection{Quality/speed Pareto frontier}
\label{sec:results-quality-pareto}

Pairing each bridge-width point in Figure~\ref{fig:f2} with its realized
speedup from Section~\ref{sec:results-efficiency} gives the paper's
central diagram: the quality/speed Pareto frontier. Reading a design
point off the frontier is the intended use for the study --- neither
``fastest'' nor ``highest-quality'' is a specification without a
threshold, but ``highest speedup inside the $\Delta$ parity band'' is.

\figureifexists{generated/F6.pdf}{%
    F6 --- quality/speed Pareto frontier. Each point is one bridge-width
    setting $k$; the horizontal dashed line marks the \texttt{full}
    baseline and the shaded band marks $\Delta$. The rightmost point
    inside the band is the operating recommendation.%
}{fig:f6}

\subsection{Base versus instruct mechanism probe}
\label{sec:results-quality-instruct}

Instruction tuning trains the model to route context through the query
region --- exactly the region \texttt{ddi\_qf} keeps intact. The
mechanistic prediction is that \texttt{ddi\_qf} costs instruction-tuned
models less than it costs their base counterparts. Table~\ref{tab:t4}
tests this prediction with matched base/instruct pairs and reports the
effect size with variance so a null result is legible.
